layer_note: Agappei's catalogue is mostly literal: the tattvas, the colours of the elements, the letters of Om are named, and the poet states his own keys (ம is maya, சி the root). The breath layer is thin and mostly the colour table; the consciousness layer carries the turn (1660: none of this is the Lord). The social layer is the sastras (1648), the letters (1658), the sects (1663) and the rites (1666).

literal.reading: Do not swallow poison, demon within; to gain the Lord's feet, do not let the heart waver, and say nothing at all.

consciousness.reading: The inner demon, the restless mind or ego, is told to be silent: silence is the rule the whole work repeats.

literal.reading: It is the Supreme beyond the supreme; it came as the wide sea, and it alone created the netherworld and the seven worlds.
Nada is the Veda; have you seen the good dance? The foot is Shakti, and the para-bindu is nada: a stack of equations from the Saiva cosmogony.
Bindu and nada came as the real (or as the body); the five great elements became their seat.
You have seen that the four paths are the good way; but unless it is the root, it is not release.

breath.reading: மூலம் as the root centre: release only through the root of the body.

consciousness.reading: மூலம் as the source itself: the paths are good, but release is the source, not a path to it.

literal.reading: The five that begin with speech, the organs of action: hear how they came; they are an aggregate, and they are not the truth.

consciousness.reading: What is compounded is not the real self.

literal.reading: The five that begin with sound, the subtle elements, became the sastras; they are also falsehood, and I have told you the truth.

social.reading: Book-learning is put on the side of the senses and called false.

literal.reading: The five that begin with வசனம் (unclear) came in strength; the ten nadis are ten, and see that this is firm.

breath.reading: The ten nadis of the yogic body, counted as part of the map.

literal.reading: All that is cause I have told as I saw it; you have seen மாரணம் too, and all the ways in which they came.

alchemy.reading: மாரணம் may be the alchemists' 'killing' of a metal or the tantric rite of killing, listed among the things that came into being; the verse makes no claim for it.

literal.reading: The Agamas told of the six tattvas; and the unchanging mandalas came as three.

breath.reading: The three unchanging mandalas are the regions of sun, moon and fire in the body.

literal.reading: Earth is golden, and this is no ignorance; water's form is white.

breath.reading: The colour table by which the meditator places the elements in the body, as the Tirumanthiram gives it.

literal.reading: Fire is red, see that this is firm; air is blue, and I will tell you of the sky.

breath.reading: The colours are the meditator's signs for the elements in the body.

literal.reading: The sky is cloud- (or smoke-) coloured; hear how it came, let there be no defect; I have told you what is.

breath.reading: The last colour of the table, completing the elements as meditated in the body.

literal.reading: All this arose as the letter அ standing there; the letter உ joined it and it came to have form.

consciousness.reading: The first two letters of Om are the first two stages of manifestation: arising, then form.

literal.reading: The letter ம is maya, and I have told you it is impurity; the letter சி is the root, so reflect on it.

consciousness.reading: The third letter of Om is the bond, and சி, Siva's syllable, is the source; the verse states its key openly.

literal.reading: Letters and worlds, mantras and tantras: I will tell you more, and you will listen with a murmur of assent.
From the elephant to the line (unclear), and the fifty-one letters: you have seen that they are falsehood, so do not believe them true.

social.reading: The letters that are the stuff of mantra practice are denied truth.

literal.reading: The tattvas came as the whole of things; I have told you the intellect too: is it not the form of the elements?

consciousness.reading: Even buddhi is elemental, so no inner faculty is the self.

literal.reading: All these kinds are not our Lord; that kind is another, so inquire and see.

consciousness.reading: The Lord is beyond every tattva the catalogue has named, and is reached by inquiry, not by listing.

literal.reading: If sin is to end, do not keep imagining; there is no dying either: it is the sadguru's feet.

consciousness.reading: No mental image (பாவனை) of the Lord.

literal.reading: However much is said, my mind is not consoled; leaving both the conscious and the unconscious, join them and see.

consciousness.reading: Beyond both spirit and matter, seen from beyond them.

literal.reading: The six religions came of their own making; inquire and tell me the place where you stand settled.

consciousness.reading: Not which sect, but where one rests: the self's own ground.

literal.reading: The thirty-six exist, but I have told you they do not avail; if there is something else, tell it truly.

consciousness.reading: The tattvas are, but they do not help toward the one.

literal.reading: When you know yourself, you will join with nothing; I will tell you what is, the way to know yourself.

consciousness.reading: Self-knowledge, marked by non-attachment, is what the catalogue did not contain.

literal.reading: Chariyai will not do: you have seen that it gives salokam; even if you do kiriyai, nothing is gained.

social.reading: Temple worship and Agamic rite are of no account.

links.note: The Tirumanthiram gives earth gold, water white, fire red, air black and the sky smoke-coloured; Agappei's 1652 to 1654 give the same table with air as நீலம் and the sky as மஞ்சு (cloud). The Siddhar takes the Tirumanthiram's meditative table as settled doctrine and then, in 1660, says none of it is the Lord.

Both state the letter key outright: Tirumular says அ is the soul, உ the supreme, ம the impurity, சி Siva; Agappei says ம is maya and impurity and சி is the root. Neither verse needs a key to be read this way, which is what the old link to Tirumanthiram 885 lacked. They part on அ: Tirumular makes it the soul, while in 1655 Agappei makes it the first arising of everything.

The letter அ as first. The Kural uses it as a simile of priority: as அ heads the letters, the Primal Lord heads the world. Agappei makes it a stage of manifestation: all this arose as அ and took form when உ joined it. The figure is the same letter at the head of things; the Kural compares, Agappei derives, and Tirumanthiram 975 makes அ the soul, so the letter has no fixed referent across the three books.

Tirumular counts fifty-one letters, eighty-one words and the rest as the way the adhvas, the paths the soul traverses, came to be; Agappei says the fifty-one letters are falsehood and are not to be believed. The conflict holds if Tirumular's verse treats the letter-path as real; it dissolves if his count is only descriptive of what the knower must pass beyond.

Both put the three mandalas inside the apparatus of tattvas that the seeker passes through: Agappei lists 'the three unchanging mandalas' after the Agamas' six tattvas, then in 1660 says none of these is the Lord; Tirumular says those who study the three mandalas and the twenty-five and follow the path by its marks end bewildered. The link holds on the words, whatever the mandalas are decoded as.

Agappei ends his catalogue of tattvas by saying none of these is the Lord, 'that kind is another: inquire and see'; Idaikkadar asks who can point to the void and answers that only the subtle intellect can. Both deny that the ultimate can be shown as one item among others, and both hand the knowing to an inner discernment (ஆராய்ந்து, புத்தி சூக்குமம்) rather than to instruction.

Agappei says the six religions came of their own making and asks the demon where it stands settled; Tirumular says the six sects that stand in the assembly do not see the God who stands within the body. The specific point shared is not merely that sects are wrong but where they look: the crowd or the doctrine against one's own ground or body (ஆயத்துள் against காயத்துள் in Tirumular).

Sivavakkiyar gives the full ladder, sariyai to salokam, kiriyai to samipam, yoga to sarupam and jnana to sayujyam; Agappei names the first rung and says kiriyai gains nothing, and in 1676 denies yoga too. Where Sivavakkiyar grades the paths, Agappei discards all but knowing oneself.

Agappei says the five subtle elements became the sastras and that they are false; Nondi says he read many sastras, left wicked company, learned the worthy vessel and with devotees saw release. The conflict is over the worth of the sastras for the way, and it holds if Nondi's reading is one of the steps to release; it dissolves if it is only a stage he passed through, since 2313 does not say the sastras gave release.

old_links.note: The colour table is stated in both.
Held only if Tirumular's மாவெழுத்து is the letter ம, a gloss his Tamil does not fix. Replaced by Tirumanthiram 975, which states the same key in words.
The status claims about the fifty-one letters conflict in the words.
'Nothing gained' is said of kiriyai, not chariyai; the pair adds nothing that 1666 qualifies 1400 does not.
Agappei grants the first rung its fruit and values it at nothing.
Rested on reading சைவந் தனையறிந்தே as self-knowledge and on Agappei speaking of Saivam, which he does not.

1649 வசனாதி and 1658 அத்தி வரைவாடி do not construe.
